notes: Tightened definitions and added exclusion rules to improve clarity between adjacent labels in the codebook.

codes.name: access barriers
codes.definition: Structural obstacles that prevent a patient from accessing care, such as distance, transport, scheduling, language, or paperwork issues.
codes.clarification: Include any obstacle that prevents a patient from reaching the clinic, regardless of whether it's physical or logistical. Examples include no nearby clinic, inadequate public transportation, or complex scheduling procedures.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT cost concerns — those are separate issues with financial implications.

positive_examples.text: The nearest hospital is 30 miles away and requires a 3-hour bus ride, making it impossible to visit during work hours.
positive_examples.why: Distance and transport physically block accessing care.

negative_examples.text: I was unable to schedule an appointment due to the complex scheduling system online.
negative_examples.why: Transportation issue prevented access to care.

codes.name: cost concerns
codes.definition: Worry about the monetary price of care, including bills, copays, premiums, or fear of debt.
codes.clarification: Include any mention of affordability, insurance not covering enough, or skipping care because of money. Note that cost concerns can be a barrier to access but are separate from physical barriers.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT provider trust issues — those involve the relationship between patient and provider.

positive_examples.text: I skipped the follow-up visit because I couldn't afford another $200 copay.
positive_examples.why: Care was forgone specifically due to financial constraints.

negative_examples.text: The waiting room was crowded and I sat there for an hour, but it didn't affect my decision to come in.

codes.name: provider trust
codes.definition: The patient's confidence in or distrust of their clinician or the health system, including feeling heard or dismissed, doubting a diagnosis, or relying on a provider's judgment.
codes.clarification: Include any issue with the provider-client relationship, such as communication, empathy, or competence. Note that this is distinct from general satisfaction with logistics like wait times.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT general dissatisfaction with wait times — those are separate issues with systemic implications.

positive_examples.text: My doctor never listens to my concerns and always rushes through our appointments.
positive_examples.why: Expresses distrust in the provider relationship.

negative_examples.text: The waiting room was clean, comfortable, and well-stocked with amenities.
negative_examples.why: No issues with the provider or system were mentioned.

codes.name: wait times
codes.definition: Delay between seeking care and receiving it — appointment lead time or time spent waiting on the day.
codes.clarification: Include any delay beyond what is considered standard or reasonable for a given system. Note that this excludes issues with accessibility, such as no nearby clinic.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT access barriers — those are structural obstacles preventing care from being accessible in the first place.

positive_examples.text: The first available appointment was 12 weeks out, causing me to delay my treatment.
positive_examples.why: A direct delay in receiving care.

negative_examples.text: There's been a significant delay with my test results, but I'm not sure why yet.
negative_examples.why: No clear cause of the delay mentioned.
